subject: Game Theory
title: Why Firms Collude
description: A quick win: understand Why Firms Collude.

hook.text: If competitors agree to keep prices high, everyone makes more money. That's the appeal of collusion.

buildup.text: Collusion turns a competitive game into a cooperative one. Firms act as a joint monopoly.

discovery.text: OPEC is the most famous cartel: member nations agree on oil output to maintain high prices.

twist.text: Collusion is a prisoner's dilemma. Each firm profits more by secretly cutting prices while others hold.

climax.text: Cartels almost always collapse. The temptation to cheat is too strong, and cheaters often go undetected.

punchline.text: Cartels are cooperation waiting to fail.

quiz.question: Why do cartels usually collapse?
options: Each member is tempted to secretly cheat
